title: Honeywell GG1320AN ring laser gyro
note: A single-axis ring laser gyro shown from the case in: the round case and its connector, two circuit boards, the mounting plate, and under it the clear glass block with the triangular laser path, three corner mirrors (two on piezo path-length actuators, one passing light to the detector), the cathode and two anodes that drive the helium-neon discharge, and the dither motor in the centre. Frame: z up along the sensing axis (perpendicular to the block), case bottom at z = 0, centred; +Y towards mirror 2 and the detector, -Y towards the cathode, as in sam_gg1320an's labelled photo of the block. Real size in metres (88 mm across). Positions in the block are measured from that photo, scaled by its scale bar; heights inside the case are estimates (open_questions).

viewer.note: inside_flip: Internal turns the gyro over about x (the camera stays put), so the laser block, which hangs under the boards, faces the viewer

reference_model.note: No 3D model of the GG1320 found; the layout is measured from sam_gg1320an's photos.

photo_scale.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_with_major_parts_labeled1.jpg: the scale bar's end ticks at x = 283 and 765 px (50.8 mm); centre = the dither motor's hub

path.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_with_major_parts_labeled1.jpg: corners of the drawn red beam, measured and scaled by photo_scale; modelled as an equilateral triangle of circumradius 28.7 mm

block.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_with_major_parts_labeled1.jpg: flat faces 19.5 mm from the centre, corners cut off at the mirrors, centre bore 18 mm (the dither ring); thickness estimated from cathode_end_of_assembly_closeup1.jpg against the 13.7 mm cathode (±15%, perspective); its outer edges bevelled about 0.8 mm (the bright edge bands, 7-8 px wide in the labelled photo at 9.5 px/mm)

bores.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_with_major_parts_labeled1.jpg: bore walls about 24 px apart, seen through the block (estimated)

roles.mirror_2: wedged substrate, top, with the detector assembly

mirrors.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_with_major_parts_labeled1.jpg (labels "Mirror 1 with PZT", "Mirror 2 on Wedged Substrate", "Detector Assembly", "Mirror 3 with PZT"; assemblies about 95 px = 10 mm across); lengths estimated from mirrorpzt_assembly1_closeup1.jpg; the substrates are clear glass discs (laser_block_top_view1.jpg, mirrorpzt_assembly1_closeup1.jpg), drawn a little less see-through than the block so they stand apart

discharge.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_with_major_parts_labeled1.jpg (labels "Cathode" on the bottom face, "Anode 1" and "Anode 2" on the two upper faces; anode 2 under a red cover)

dither.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_with_major_parts_labeled1.jpg ("Dither Motor", zoomed round its hub at (524,404) px, 9.49 px/mm): a cloverleaf inside the ring: a hub 7.4 mm across with a 1.7 mm hole, three lobes 5.5 mm out towards the three mirrors, each about 4.4 x 8.7 mm with a 3.4 mm hole, and three thin spokes to the ring between them (towards the cathode and anodes) carrying the piezo plates; frequency from the unit's label in top_view_of_complete_rlg1.jpg

connector_bars.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_with_major_parts_labeled1.jpg ("Connector BC1", "Connector BC2": white bars beside the upper faces); height estimated

stack.source: sam_gg1320an, estimated: the block hangs under the mounting plate from the dither hub (three screws at the plate's centre, interior_after_separating_case1.jpg), the two boards sit in the top half (pcb1_pcb2_in_situ1.jpg); heights chosen to fit the 45 mm case

connector.source: honeywell_gg1320an, p.1: "RS-422, 25 pin micro \"D\""; flange width from sam_gg1320an, top_view_of_complete_rlg1.jpg (scaled by the 88 mm case, 895 px: 10.2 px/mm): the CINCH flange spans 305-628 px; the rest from sam_gg1320an, main_connector1.jpg (scaled by the 31.8 mm flange, 900 px: 28.3 px/mm): receptacle 605 px wide at its top, 580 px at its bottom, 155 px tall, contacts in rows of 12 and 13 at 38.4 px pitch, rows 30 px apart, jackscrews 750 px apart and 90 px across; rise of the shell and jackscrews above the flange and the place on the can estimated (the connector faces up out of the cover's window)

performance.quote: 1,164,352 ±18 pulses/rev. ... 0.0035 deg/hr (typical) ... 900 deg/ sec (maximum ) ... 1 lb. (454 grams)

pad.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_bottom_view1.jpg: a dark lattice pad on the block's plate side, strips along the three faces, a ring round the dither motor, spokes to the face centres and a window at each corner; sizes estimated against the block (19.5 mm faces)

corner_wells.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_with_major_parts_labeled1.jpg: a wide bore along each corner's bisector, from the mirror inward (the top one ends 9.5 mm above the centre; about 60 px across); not labelled, purpose not stated

discharge_channels.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_with_major_parts_labeled1.jpg: thin bores from the cathode (two, side by side) and from each anode to the beam bores; diameter estimated

cathode_flange.source: sam_gg1320an, cathode_end_of_assembly_closeup1.jpg: a flange where the cathode meets the block, a gold-coloured seal ring and a solder tab with a hole; scaled by the 13.7 mm cathode (estimated)

anode_2_cover.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_top_on_plate1.jpg (ruler: 1 in = 257 px, 10.1 px/mm; the photo is the labelled view turned 180°): anode 2's red cover 85 px wide; height estimated

detector.source: sam_gg1320an, mirror_detector_assembly2_closeup1.jpg: the detector potted in grey rubber over mirror 2, two photodiode packages ("Fringe Sensor Photodiodes") side by side with three gold pins each, an amber epoxy blob over the left one; scaled by the 10 mm mirror (estimated)

plate.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_top_on_plate1.jpg (ruler: 1 in = 257 px, 10.1 px/mm; the photo is the labelled view turned 180°): plate edges cut straight behind mirrors 1 and 3 (35 mm from the centre) and behind the cathode (24.3 mm), six screw holes; interior_after_separating_case1.jpg: screws in aluminium washers, three screws at the centre (the dither hub)

housing.source: sam_gg1320an, pcb1_pcb2_in_situ1.jpg and interior_after_separating_case1.jpg: an aluminium cup holding the boards above the plate; sizes estimated to fit the case; its top meets the can's top plate (facts.cover)

pcb_parts.source: sam_gg1320an, pcb1_pcb2_in_situ1.jpg: the two boards side by side (pcb2 about 6.3 px/mm, pcb1 about 5.8 px/mm, scaled by their 74 mm and 64 mm widths, estimated): pcb2 with an 84-lead PLCC, a 100-lead QFP and a header; pcb1 D-shaped with a hybrid module ("PRECISION INC"), a header and small parts; joined by an orange flex cable. Which way each board faces, and how they turn against the block, is estimated; the two large chips' lead rows stand 0.75 mm out from their bodies (estimated)

wires.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_bottom_view1.jpg: red, white and black wires from the connector bars to the anodes, mirrors and detector; routes simplified

case_shape.source: sam_gg1320an, bottom_view_of_complete_rlg1.jpg: a raised disc 71 mm across on the bottom (scaled by the 88 mm case), step height estimated; top_view_of_complete_rlg1.jpg: the label covers a disc about 65 mm across

cover.source: sam_gg1320an, top_view_of_complete_rlg1.jpg (scaled by the 88 mm case, 895 px: 10.2 px/mm) and top_with_outer_cover_removed1.jpg: the top cover is a black cup over an aluminium can; a window in it, cut straight 29 mm from the centre (label's lower edge at 530 px) out to the rim, shows the can's top with the connector; a round peg sticks out of the can below the connector. Depths estimated

cover_screws.source: sam_gg1320an, top_view_of_complete_rlg1.jpg (a screw at the label's centre, about 32 px across: 3.1 mm) and bottom_view_of_complete_rlg1.jpg (one at the bottom's centre)

mount_notches.source: sam_gg1320an, bottom_view_of_complete_rlg1.jpg (scaled by the 88 mm case, 910 px: 10.3 px/mm): a notch in the bottom rim under the connector, 300 px wide, with a V-shaped aluminium pad and a 30 px hole in its roof, and two more at the sides; bottom_with_outer_cover_removed1.jpg: the can's mounting flats with holes at two sides. Spacing taken as 120° (the photo is oblique), the V's depth and the notch height estimated

hub_nuts.source: sam_gg1320an, with_custom_umbilical_cable1.jpg: three hex nuts on the dither motor's free side, about 90 px across corners against the 245 px (18 mm) ring: 6.6 mm (5.7 mm across flats, taken as 5.5); placed on the lobes' holes (labelled photo), which the bolts pass through

discharge_path.source: sam_gg1320an, powered_view1-3.jpg: the discharge glows from each anode down its channel, along the side bore to the bottom corner (mirror 1 or 3), along the bottom bore and up the two cathode channels; the bore halves next to mirror 2 stay dark. Drawn in three layers like the photos: a blown-out yellow-white core, the orange glow, and a faint red haze spreading into the glass. Radii, brightness and see-through chosen by eye; the glowing layers have a black surface so the scene's lights don't wash them out. The laser beam itself can't be seen in a real gyro: it's drawn as a thin red line

pzt_end.source: sam_gg1320an, mirrorpzt_assembly1_closeup1.jpg (scaled by the 10 mm assembly, 530 px: 53 px/mm): the path-length assembly ends in a metal housing with a white ceramic disc (330 px), a dark ring round its centre hole (180 px; bore 100 px), an orange flex in a horseshoe round the lower part with a solder tab each side and a solder blob at the bottom; housing length estimated; the housing's front has a raised rim (outer 10% of the radius) with a dark groove inside it (to 84%), the ceramic recessed below the rim (mirrorpzt_assembly1_closeup1.jpg, mirror_pzt_assembly3_closeup1.jpg; ratios and heights estimated)

temperature_sensor.source: sam_gg1320an, laser_block_with_major_parts_labeled1.jpg ("Temperature Sensor", pointing at (630,155) px: on anode 1's face, 17.2 mm from its centre towards mirror 2); temperature_sensor_ad590_cloesup1.jpg ("AD590KF" printed on a flat package, long side across the block; size estimated against the 1.5 mm channel above it)

open_questions: Heights inside the case (block, plate, boards) are estimates: no photo shows the stack from the side.
Block thickness (12 mm) is estimated from a close-up with perspective; the block's glass type isn't stated anywhere found.
The corner wells (wide bores at each corner) aren't labelled in any photo found: purpose unknown.
Board parts are placed from one oblique photo; which way the boards face and turn against the block is estimated.
The top cover's window depth, the can's top height and the connector's rise above it are estimated.
The mounting notches' spacing (120°), V depth and height are estimated from oblique photos.
